title: Revel Bikes Went Big with the El Jefe Grande 32er
content:
Revel Bikes went big with the El Jefe Grande, a 32er version of its beloved titanium hardtail. The El Jefe has been a staple of the Revel lineup since 2020, and riders have taken it everywhere from local singletrack to multi-week bikepacking routes. Now there’s a bigger one.
Meet the El Jefe Grande, built on the same do-it-all spirit as the original 29er.

Titanium runs deep at Revel. The same founding team launched Why Cycles in 2016 with the mission of making bikes with “a modern take on traditional titanium.” Why Bikes merged with Revel in 2023, and that original mission has driven the titanium program ever since. John lauded the Revel Tirade, and it remains one of his favorite bikes to date.

Revel first debuted a 32er prototype at Sea Otter this year as part of its Concept Labs program, but the finished production bike is a different animal. Getting there took more prototypes, a lot of riding, and completely reworked geometry to handle the unique characteristics of the extra-big wheels.

El Jefe Grande Quick Hits

  • $3,499 USD
  • Proper modern geometry, dialed specifically for 32″ wheels
  • Extra-clean internal cable routing
  • Sliding dropouts with 17mm of adjustment for tuning wheelbase or running singlespeed
  • UDH-compatible titanium dropouts, the same as other Revel Ti models
  • Plenty of bottle and accessory mounts, five sets on every size
  • A 3D-printed head tube, smooth-welded to the top and down tubes, a first for a production Revel

The new head tube design is for more than just good looks. Revel has been experimenting with 3D-printed titanium for several years, and the 32er platform is where it matters most. Big wheels mean short head tubes paired with a long 32er-wheel fork, and that long lever arm puts a lot of force into the front of the frame. Standard titanium welding techniques generally don’t provide the strength needed there. The 3D-printed head tube is extremely burly and ISO-tested beyond standard mountain bike requirements. The result is a significantly stiffer, stronger, and more durable front end. It also opens up even cleaner cable routing options.

The frame is designed around a 100 mm fork and comes in four sizes. Medium through XL run 32″ wheels front and rear. The size small pairs a 32″ front with a 29″ rear. A size large frame weighs 4.76 lb (2.16 kg), and the complete bike as shown below comes in at 24.9 lb (11.29 kg).

Price? The El Jefe Grande 32er retails for $3,499 USD. Reserve now with a $500 deposit at Revel Bikes.
